title: Hierarchical Crews: Managed Delegation
objective: After this lesson you will be able to run hierarchical crews with manager delegation, budget rounds and depth, prove termination, and decide sequential vs hierarchical per workflow with recorded reasons.
why: Some work can't be sequenced upfront: fraud checks sometimes, VIP handling on signals, escalation when stuck. Hierarchical crews delegate per-step judgment to a manager — flexible at the price of traceability and termination risk. This lesson makes management explicit (budgets, proofs, audits) instead of emergent and hopeful.

blocks.text: The **manager** observes shared state and assigns the next worker: same routing discipline as LangGraph Ch.4 (enumerated branches, fallbacks, confidence gates), plus delegation history (who did what, already tried). Real CrewAI: `Crew(process=Process.hierarchical, manager_llm=...)` — the manager role exists in-framework; this lesson teaches operating it.

blocks.caption: Rounds-bounded delegation: exhaustion escalates, loops terminate

blocks.text: Every managed loop needs **two** terminators: **max rounds** (hard cap — exhaustion escalates to human with full history) and a **done condition** the manager can actually observe (verdict field set, all checklist items passed). Prove termination before running: trace the worst case on paper (each round either sets done or consumes budget). Loops without proofs hang on the first ambiguous case.

blocks.caption: Done-conditions are stated, observable, and quoted back each round

blocks.text: Manager audits: who delegated what, why

Managers need oversight too: log every assignment with its **reason** (state snapshot + chosen worker + why-others-not). Review delegation traces for loops (A→B→A patterns), bias (favorite worker overuse), and budget burn rate. A manager whose reasons don't reference state is improvising — constrain with the routing-table discipline from Ch.4 of LangGraph.

blocks.title: Budget the manager
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok=true rounds=2 with history checker,drafter — then loop guard ok=false budget-exhausted at 3 rounds. Sync twin of production async: identical budget/termination logic. Termination by construction in both directions: done-flags finish work, budgets finish loops.

items: Managers delegate per-step with history; budgets (rounds) + done-conditions terminate every loop
Done patterns stated and quoted each round; exhaustion escalates with full history, never hangs
Audit delegation traces for loops, bias, burn rate — managers get oversight too

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice manager and record both outcomes. (b) Remove the done branch from the manager (always return checker) and confirm budget-exhaustion at the cap. (c) Write the done-condition for a returns flow (verdict + draft + log present) and state where the manager reads each signal.
hints: Baseline: ok=true rounds=2 (checker, drafter); broken manager: ok=false reason budget-exhausted rounds=3.
Done-condition: state.verdict && state.draft && state.logged → done. Signals read from shared state channels (Ch.2 LangGraph state design).
The broken-manager run proves budgets work independently of manager quality — termination is structural.
exercise.why: Breaking the manager on purpose proves termination is structural (budgets), not behavioral (good management). Done-conditions tie completion to observable state, the only kind that works.
exercise.code: // Termination-proof pattern: cap + observable done-condition, tested both ways.

options: Termination: max rounds + observable done-condition — unbounded delegation hangs
quiz.explain: Dynamic delegation cycles without structural exits. Caps bound damage; done-conditions finish work; both tested.

quiz.q: Budget exhausted with full history. Correct handling?
options: Escalate to human with the complete trail — exhaustion is a designed terminal with evidence
quiz.explain: Exhaustion carries the full delegation history to a human: what was tried, what remains. Designed terminal, not failure.

quiz.q: Sequential vs hierarchical for VIP dispute handling?
options: Hierarchical: per-case routing (fraud check sometimes, VIP handling on signals) needs step judgment — with recorded variability reason
quiz.explain: Variability decides: conditional steps need managed delegation. Record the reason — topology choices need justifications.

summary: Managed delegation with history, budgets + done-conditions as termination proofs, audited assignments. Hierarchy for variability, sequential for fixed flows — decided per workflow, recorded always.
next: Managed or pipelined, agents share work through boards: ownership, handoffs, and the states that prevent double-work. Next: the task board.
